articles.title: 'Our worst nightmare': Threats to Australian politicians were rising before MP hit by car
articles.description: In the wake of the apparent attack on MP Helen Haines, MPs have described locking their office doors, and scanning every crowd for potential threats.

articles.title: Oil-Rich Alberta Votes on its Future in Canada
articles.description: Electors have been asked if they wish to remain in Canada or to hold another vote on breaking away in a referendum that left both sides unhappy.

articles.title: Deaths at Danjiri Float Festival Prompt Questions in Japan
articles.description: The vibrant danjiri tradition dates back three centuries, but two recent fatalities have prompted anxiety over whether participants can remain safe.

articles.title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget
articles.description: Influential Labour figures had been pushing for equalising CGT and income tax, but critics have said this could drive wealthy people out of Britain.

articles.title: Trump’s Push for Deals With Russia Powers His Frustration With Ukraine
articles.description: The series of recent steps by the president that seem to favor Vladimir Putin reflect his intensifying desire to normalize the relationship with Moscow even if it means further undercutting Ukraine.

articles.title: Gilbert Bigio, Haitian Tycoon Linked to Gangs, Dies at 91
articles.description: Reportedly the wealthiest man in the poorest country in the Western Hemisphere, Gilbert Bigio was sanctioned for ties to criminal gangs. He was 91.

articles.title: US church on frontline of battle against drug known as 'tranq'
articles.description: Synthetic opioids like fentanyl are more powerful and in plentiful supply, and they have transformed the drugs landscape.

articles.title: France in Shock After Protests Turn Into Riots, Damaging Buildings and Shops
articles.description: After anti-government protests devolved into chaos, leaders from across the political spectrum blamed one another for the unrest, even as it largely subsided on Sunday.

articles.title: Albania’s Leader, Edi Rama, Denounces Violent Protests
articles.description: Students upset by living and educational costs have revived protests. Prime Minister Edi Rama said they were being used by “outside forces.”

articles.title: Kenya Confirms Four New Ebola Cases
articles.description: Seven Ebola infections have now been confirmed in Kenya, which before this month had never recorded cases of the deadly virus.

articles.title: Deadly ‘Incident’ at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright Sparks Fire
articles.description: The defense minister said people were killed and injured at a base in Alberta, but officials did not offer details on the cause.

articles.title: Pope Leo Leaves Hospital, Days After Lung Cancer Surgery
articles.description: Leo XIV had been treated for lung cancer at Gemelli Hospital in Rome.

articles.title: Unrest Mars Day of Protest in France, as Student Movement Turns National
articles.description: Riots broke out in several French cities alongside peaceful marches of tens of thousands of people demonstrating against rising living costs and poor school conditions.

articles.title: Egypt’s Defense Chiefs Pledge to Support Saudi Arabia After Houthi Attacks
articles.description: President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi had called on Egyptian lawmakers to authorize military assistance to the kingdom, saying any support would be defensive.

articles.title: Zelensky Says Trump Risks ‘Historic Mistake’ If He Backs Russia
articles.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine pressed Sunday for more information on possible restrictions to Starshield, a U.S.-provided satellite internet service used by the Ukrainian military.

articles.title: In India, the Scion of a Political Dynasty Tries to Seize His Moment
articles.description: Rahul Gandhi is the descendant of three prime ministers. A surge of protests could give him a springboard to take on the nation’s current leader.

articles.title: At Least 19 Dead After Stampede at Indian Religious Event
articles.description: Such deadly crowd events are relatively common in India, and it was unclear what caused this one. The authorities detained the event’s organizer and others involved.

articles.title: Israeli Settlers Attack Palestinians and European Officials in West Bank
articles.description: Extremists assaulted residents and broke a European diplomatic vehicle’s window, witnesses said, as settler violence surges in the territory during the olive harvest.

articles.title: Dispute Between Trump Allies Centers on Millions Transferred From Congo
articles.description: The White House inquiry is focused on diverging accounts from Richard Grenell and Alina Habba Mildon about a $17 million transfer from a government account in the African country to a Texas defense firm.

articles.title: Mexican Judge Sentences 3 Men to 159 Years Each in Surfer Killings
articles.description: The men were charged in the murders of two Australians and an American who were on a camping and surf vacation in Mexico.

articles.title: What to Know About the Violent Protests in Albania
articles.description: Student demonstrations over education converged with broader protests against rising living costs and a luxury development linked to Jared Kushner, President Trump’s son-in-law.

articles.title: Egypt’s President Says He Will Leave Office in 2030
articles.description: President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, who has so far ruled for over a dozen years, pledged to respect constitutional limits while also seeking parliamentary approval to help defend Saudi Arabia.

articles.title: U.S. Floats Lifeline to Russia: Allowing More Gas Sales to Europe
articles.description: The Trump administration is pitching the idea as part of a peace deal with Ukraine, but Europe is wary and critics say Russia would be strengthened.

articles.title: Yemen Fighting Rages as Civilian Toll From Houthi-Saudi Conflict Worsens
articles.description: New clashes were reported as the Houthis put more pressure on Taiz, a city connecting the government-held south of the country and the Red Sea.

articles.title: Indian Gen Z Protest Leader Is Released on Bail After Arrest
articles.description: Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, was detained on his way to a protest called to demand the resignation of India’s top election official.

articles.title: A Calgary Crowd Rallies for Canada as Alberta’s Vote on Secession Nears
articles.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney was among the speakers calling for a united Canada and warning about the dangers of division.

articles.title: 'The French correction' and 'Labour cuts £2bn from Army'
articles.description: Violent unrest in France continues and Defence drops funding for frontline military vehicles lead Tuesday's papers.

articles.title: England coach should be English, suggests Fleming
articles.description: New Zealander Stephen Fleming, England’s new Test coach, suggests the national team should be led by someone from England.

articles.title: Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?
articles.description: After every round of Premier League matches this season, Troy Deeney gives us his team of the week. Do you agree with his choices?

articles.title: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits
articles.description: The families of the victims of Nottingham killer Valdo Calocane had been campaigning for the change.

articles.title: I have a condition people are too embarrassed to talk about
articles.description: Women share their experience of lichen sclerosus.

articles.title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world
articles.description: As the strongest El Niño on record continues to intensify, what impacts on weather patterns are already being felt across the globe? Sarah Keith-Lucas looks at the evidence.

articles.title: The singles choosing in-person dating events over apps
articles.description: The BBC hears from people who think dating events are better value for money than dating apps.

articles.title: Priest in Ecuador Dies After Crucifix Falls on Him During Livestreamed Mass
articles.description: The Rev. Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari was addressing his congregation in Guayaquil, Ecuador, when a wooden cross detached from a wall and struck him.

articles.title: Maddison's magic moment for Spurs - 18 months in the making
articles.description: On his first start since May 2025, James Maddison provided the moment of magic Tottenham were waiting for in their 3-1 victory against Coventry, writes Phil McNulty.

articles.title: The French Teen Maimed During School Unrest by Tear Gas Grenade
articles.description: The police’s treatment of the student last month sheds light on how a wave of school unrest evolved into national protests that spilled into widespread riots on Saturday.

articles.title: Coast Guard Halts Search for Survivors of Capsized Boat Off Mexico
articles.description: Some 11 people were missing but 16 were rescued, including three who had injuries consistent with shark bites, the authorities said.

articles.title: Cult Leader Convicted of Mass Murder by Court in Kenya
articles.description: Paul Nthenge Mackenzie told his doomsday followers in a remote forest to fast for salvation. He faced trial after hundreds of bodies were exhumed.

articles.title: Italy Faces Parallel Protests in the North and South
articles.description: Protests by young people in northern cities ended in riots as farmers and truckers in the south, angered by high gas prices, stopped commercial traffic.

articles.title: Ronaldo given 30-day suspension and £215 fine by Portuguese FA
articles.description: Cristiano Ronaldo is given a 30-day suspension by the Portuguese Football Federation after leaving his country's international camp last month.

articles.title: Spurs beat Coventry to earn first league win of the season
articles.description: Tottenham Hotspur record their first Premier League win of the season and move off the bottom of the table with a home victory over Coventry City.

articles.title: Watch: Clean up begins after French riots but police remain
articles.description: Outside of Paris, Marseille saw some of the worst damage, with shop owners reporting more than 600 premises having been looted.

articles.title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules
articles.description: Penalties are seen as too harsh on motorists who are penalised for parking on private land.

articles.title: Curfew imposed in parts of central Paris and other cities after rioting across France
articles.description: It comes after the country's interior minister admits that police "lost control" in some cities.

articles.title: Ex-OpenAI worker accused of planting device had Saudi support, says court filing
articles.description: The Saudi government did not immediately respond to BBC requests for comment.

articles.title: Maddison shines on return - Tottenham v Coventry ratings
articles.description: How Spurs and Coventry City's players rated following their Premier League match.

articles.title: Tennis star Svitolina says emotional toll of Ukraine war led to Monfils separation
articles.description: The two top tennis pros married in 2021 and have one child together.

articles.title: Ukrainians dying because US restricting intelligence sharing, Zelensky adviser tells BBC
articles.description: Serhii Beskrestnov says there has not been enough time to warn people about incoming missile attacks. The White House said there had been no changes to intelligence sharing.
